title: When using set_script in a tool, depending on the script, when setting properties, errors can occur
body: ### Tested versions v4.6.3.stable.official [7d41c59c4] ### System information not relevant ### Issue description Hi, I'm encoutering a weird error when using set_script in a `@tool` script. I'm assigning a script to a node I receive from elsewhere, and when I try to set a property's value, I have this error: ```error Invalid assignment of property or key 'instance_id' with value of type 'int' on a base object of type 'StaticBody3D (MultiMeshInstanceCollider)'. ``` The code: ``` @tool class_name MyClass # etc # collider is a StaticBody3D I obtain from elsewhere if collider: collider.set_script(MultiMeshInstanceCollider) #collider.set_script("MultiMeshInstanceCollider") print("is right class ", is_instance_of(collider, MultiMeshInstanceCollider)) print("script ", collider.get_script()) #collider.instance_id = id collider.toto = "yeah" collider.get_parent().remove_child(collider) SceneUtils.add_child(colliders_container, collider) collider.instance_id = id ``` The class: ```python #@tool extends StaticBody3D class_name MultiMeshInstanceCollider #@export var instance_id: int = 0 @export var toto: String = "" func _ready() -> void: print("I am ready") ``` For the class on which the script is attached to: If `@tool` is on the instanced class: no errors, regardless of `@export` (can be present, can be absent) If `@tool` is not present, if `@export` is not present: error, if present: no error If `@tool` is on class, _ready is called If not `@tool` on class: _ready is not called The [doc](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_object.html#class-object-method-set-script) indicates: > Attaches script to the object, and instantiates it. As a result, the script's [_init()](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_object.html#class-object-private-method-init) is called. Which does not seem to be the case if `@tool` is not present, in the editor, I'm not sure if this is normal, so it's either a bug or should be in the documentation. Possible duplicates / connected: * https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/98290 is not the same, but looks similar * https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/112225 same error but not the same situation * https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/38373 looks similar but is different ### Steps to reproduce Create the two classes, click on the button. Comment and uncomment the `@tool` and `@export` annotations to see what changes. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) This is reproducing the errors: Add a script with this code, and the other class. ```python @tool extends Node3D class_name Toto @export_tool_button("generate") var instancing_something_button = instancing_something func instancing_something(): var toto = StaticBody3D.new() toto.set_script(MultiMeshInstanceCollider) if toto is MultiMeshInstanceCollider: toto.toto = "yo" toto.instance_id = 3 add_child(self, toto) static func add_child(parent: Node, child: Node) -> Node: if not parent: return null parent.add_child(child) var owner = parent if Engine.is_editor_hint(): owner = parent.get_tree().edited_scene_root set_owner(child, owner) return child ```
